summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that theism-atheism debate is distorted by epistemic rules (parsimony, verifiability, burden of proof) that secretly encode ethical commitments. It critiques Shalkowski and Scriven, uses Hegel to expose communicative failure, and resolves by rejecting both foundationalism and relativism in favor of dialectical transcendence through reciprocal interrogation.
